devpost_first_sections: What happens if you reverse-engineer the mouth movements that a piece of audio implies? Real speech comes from a tongue, jaw, and lips that have physical speed limits. A human tongue tip tops out around 20 cm/s during natural speech. TTS models don't simulate a mouth. They learn acoustic patterns and reproduce them, and the articulator movements their audio implies are often biomechanically impossible. LARYNX reconstructs those implied movements, measures their velocities, and renders the result inside a 3D skull cross-section. Velocity Computation: It computes velocities frame by frame to determine how fast each articulator would need to move between consecutive positions. Real speech stays within biomechanical limits. Deepfakes don't. Inspector is an MCP server that gives your coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP client) the ability to autonomously test the app it just built. It launches your app in a cloud sandbox, uses computer-use to operate it like a real user (screenshots, element detection, clicks), and maps the UI into regions. Each region gets its own agent that tests in parallel. Findings are independently verified with 2-of-2 replay agreement, de-duplicated, and sent back as a structured fix list. The coding agent patches the code and Inspector re-verifies. It works across web, Electron, Android, and iOS through pure pixel-level interaction. MediLedger is all about collaboration: providing a decentralized platform on which hospitals can more securely and confidently transmit sensitive data. From our experience at festivals, it became apparent that these were perfect cases where a lot of trash is left behind on the ground and significant human work is needed to clean the venues. Inspired by the boom in software automation of many tasks, we wanted to extend this to robots. We wanted to go beyond simply monitoring and identifying trash using computer vision, and make an immediate impact by acting. And what better way to do that than to clean the trash ourselves. Our lofty goal for this hackathon became to build an autonomou

Our FestiCleaner robot fully autonomously identifies, locates, pathfinds to, picks up, and returns trash to a garbage collection unit. The robot monitors and collects temperature, humidity, and video data during its operation. This data is relayed in real-time to an interactive dashboard, where a user can view the robot's operations in an annotated live video feed, track its trash-cleaning progress, view its sensor data, and remotely turn it on or off.

glance.what: AI security tool that detects, validates, and fixes code vulnerabilities, with a benchmark of models.
glance.why: Finds and fixes security flaws in code with AI agents, backed by a benchmark.

record.what_it_is: A security platform for AI agents: ECVE-Bench, a benchmark of real GitHub-advisory vulnerabilities across ecosystems, a security-tuned agent harness with sandboxed tools, a live results dashboard, and a Devin-driven loop that reproduces, patches and opens PRs for findings.

record.problem_statement: Open-source supply-chain attacks are rising and existing tools and benchmarks are not built for agents or modern ecosystems.
record.devpost_tagline: AI-Native CyberSec — detect, validate, and fix vulnerabilities with agent intelligence, powered by an open harness and an expansive benchmark

glance.what: AI glasses that auto-write listings with condition reports, plus recommendations for homes and cars.
glance.for_whom: buyers and sellers of homes and cars
glance.why: Creates verified listings from what the glasses see and matches buyers to items they like.

record.what_it_is: Smart glasses record short videos of a car or property; a locally trained YOLO model detects damage and features and produces a structured listing with a condition score. A React app lets buyers browse listings and chat with an agent that matches natural-language wishes to listings.
record.problem_and_user: Home and car buyers who cannot tell the real condition from hand-written listings.
record.one_line_pitch: Smart-glasses video is analyzed by a YOLO model to auto-build car and property listings with condition scores, plus an AI chat that recommends matching listings.
record.target_user: car and home buyers and listing creators
record.problem_statement: Online car and property listings rely on subjective descriptions, so buyers cannot easily judge real condition.
record.devpost_tagline: VisionScout: a bridge between what you see and want. AI glasses auto-generate listings with condition reports, and an AI gives you Spotify-level recommendations for homes and cars that fit your vibe.
devpost_first_sections: VisionScout 👓 "See Smarter. Decide Faster."

Every car or property listing you see online is written by someone trying to describe what they saw — and every buyer is left trying to imagine what’s real. We thought: Why are listings still manually written in 2025? What if your glasses could do the listing for you — detecting condition, estimating confidence, and automatically generating a full summary? And what if you could then talk to an AI assistant that understood your preferences and taste — giving you Spotify-level recommendations for homes or cars that fit your vibe, budget, and lifestyle? That’s how VisionScout was born: a bridge between what your eyes see and what your heart wants — where visual data meets personalized discovery

glance.why: Automates product busywork and turns strategy into shippable stories faster.

record.what_it_is: A multi-agent LLM command center for product managers covering discovery through deprecation. It turns goals and KPIs into Jira or Azure DevOps ready stories, keeps Confluence pages linked, and runs an operate loop that proposes backlog changes, with a human approving.
record.problem_and_user: Product managers losing hours to copy-paste between Jira/ADO, Confluence and chat, with strategy and KPIs not reaching stories.
record.one_line_pitch: Multi-agent LLM command center that links product-management tools and turns strategy and KPIs into Jira/ADO-ready stories.
record.problem_statement: PMs waste time on copy-paste glue across Jira, Confluence and chats, and strategy rarely flows into backlog stories.
record.devpost_tagline: ProDuh! is a multi-agent, LLM-powered command center for PMs. It unifies Discovery→Operate, works with Jira/ADO, automates busywork, and turns strategy into shippable stories—fast.

Migrations (e.g., Jira ↔ ADO) create tool chaos and duplicated work. Lost in pages: decisions and context get buried across dozens of Confluence/Docs pages—ProDuh anchors a single canonical page per phase, auto-links related artifacts, and keeps My Notes attached so nothing gets lost. We wanted an AI layer that removes busywork so PMs can focus on decisions and people. 🖥️ What it does Multi-agent, LLM-powered command center for the PM lifecycle: Discovery → Strategy → Backlog → Jira Enhancements → GTM → Release → Operate. App-agnostic

glance.why: Improves workout form and counts reps so exercise is safer and more effective.

glance.what: Job search app that serves job listings through short vertical video reels.
glance.for_whom: job seekers who scroll short video
glance.why: Makes job searching feel like scrolling reels, so applying is quicker and more engaging.

record.problem_and_user: Job seekers, especially Gen Z, tired of walls of text and repeated form filling.
record.one_line_pitch: Mobile app that turns job listings into short vertical videos you swipe through, with semantic matching to your profile.
record.problem_statement: Job hunting means reading walls of text and repetitive applications, unlike effortless short-form video browsing.
record.devpost_tagline: Why apply to jobs when you can just watch some reels?

Job hunting sucks. You scroll through endless walls of text, copy-paste the same resume into a dozen forms, and still hear nothing back. Meanwhile, we spend hours on TikTok and Instagram Reels consuming content effortlessly. We asked ourselves: what if finding your next job felt as easy as scrolling through Reels? Gen Z and millennials already consume information through short-form video. Why should job discovery be stuck in the 2010s? ReelJobs brings job listings into the format we actually enjoy consuming.

glance.what: College app that matches friends' free time and coordinates spontaneous hangouts and club dues.
glance.why: Makes it easy to find friends who are free and plan hangouts without endless texting.

record.what_it_is: A native iOS app for UNC Chapel Hill students that shows when friends are free, imports a class schedule, lets users post plans and join clubs, and puts a free-now answer on Home and Lock Screen widgets. It syncs through Firebase and works offline via a local cache.
record.problem_and_user: First-year and other college students who struggle to find mutual free time, discover clubs and keep track of meetings and dues across posters and group chats.
record.one_line_pitch: iOS campus app that finds mutual free time among friends, tracks course schedules and helps students discover clubs, meeting times and dues.
record.problem_statement: College life is scattered across posters, chats and calendars, so students miss events and hangouts.
record.devpost_tagline: CampusSync streamlines college life by matching friends' free time, coordinating spontaneous hangouts, and tracking club meetings and dues.
devpost_first_sections: As a first-year college student, navigating campus life is overwhelming. The lightbulb moment came when my brother asked for my schedule on Google Calendar, and we instantly saw our mutual free times. It made me realize how convenient it is to know when peers are free to grab food or hang out. I wanted to build an app that eliminates the friction of scheduling, alongside the headache of tracking campus clubs and dues—tasks that shouldn't cause students unnecessary stress.

CampusSync is an all-in-one student platform that centralizes college life. It automatically maps out mutual free time between friends for spontaneous hangouts, tracks course schedules, and unifies campus organization life. It makes discovering clubs effortless for first-years and simplifies tracking meeting times and paying dues, replacing chaotic posters, missed club fairs, and endless group chats.

glance.what: AI virtual nurse that talks through health concerns, remembers past chats, and helps find care.
glance.why: Guides people through health worries and connects them to care when needed.

record.what_it_is: A voice and video virtual nurse that holds a natural conversation, tracks symptoms over time, searches the web and nearby hospitals, can book appointments through browser automation and email follow-ups, and hands a clinical summary to a provider.
record.problem_and_user: Patients facing slow, repetitive intake and confusing care, plus clinics that want structured pre-visit data.
record.one_line_pitch: Voice and video virtual nurse that listens, reads the camera feed and interprets symptoms in real time.
record.problem_statement: Patients need quick, attentive first-line symptom triage without waiting for a nurse.
record.devpost_tagline: Lotus AI is an agentic virtual nurse that empathetically guides users through health concerns, remembers past interactions, and proactively helps them find care when needed.
devpost_first_sections: We’ve all been there: sitting in a waiting room, filling out endless forms, and getting blindsided by a big bill just to hear, “It’s the flu.” We thought, why does healthcare have to be this complicated? That’s why we built Lotus , an intelligent triage AI that makes healthcare feel human again. No paperwork. No waiting rooms. Just a simple, natural conversation about how you’re feeling. Lotus listens, asks the right questions, and delivers a clean, complete clinical summary straight to your provider. You shouldn’t have to repeat your story five times to get care. Lotus empowers doctors. Clinics get more accurate data, faster visits, and lower costs. Patients get clarity, shorter waits, and

Lotus AI is your virtual nurse. It is attentive, fast, and always ready. It listens to your voice, interprets your video feed, and understands your symptoms in real time. Lotus AI can also access your location, search the web, and even book show dialogs to book an appointment. Then, it helps you take the next best step. glance.what: Tool that turns your ideas into stories so you can start building.
glance.why: Helps people move from ideas to stories so they can start building sooner.

record.problem_and_user: Product managers and teams spending time converting scattered documentation into a backlog.
record.one_line_pitch: Backend that ingests a product's documentation into a RAG store and generates structured epics and tasks for Jira from it.
record.problem_statement: Product managers spend heavy manual effort turning scattered documents into an actionable backlog.
record.devpost_tagline: Turn your ideas into stories. Stop Reading. Start Building.
devpost_first_sections: Recognizing the major bottleneck for today’s product teams - the tedious manual effort required to turn scattered documentation into a clear, actionable backlog - we created id8, a smart API backend designed to streamline the process. id8 ingests all of a product’s existing knowledge base and automatically organizes it into structured epics and tasks, giving product managers more time to focus on strategy, decision-making, and team leadership, instead of wrestling with paperwork.

id8 is an intelligent API designed to serve as a product manager's right hand. By taking in all your product’s key documents - PDFs, DOCX files, and text notes - it organizes this information into clear, actionable Jira user stories and epics. With a single call to its /generate-epics endpoint, id8 gathers relevant details from across your knowledge base and turns them into a prioritized list of software epics, complete with helpful descriptions and acceptance criteria. This makes planning and backlog creation fast, reliable, and easy.

glance.what: Analysis tool that examines how traders behave to reveal patterns in their trading.
glance.why: Shows traders their own behavior patterns so they can improve decisions.

record.what_it_is: Solo-built platform where a trader uploads a CSV of trade history and gets behavioral-bias analysis (revenge trading, overtrading, loss spirals) plus a chat-style AI coach and downloadable PDF report. Uses layered detection from rules to a small ML model to an LLM.
record.problem_and_user: Retail traders who know their strategy but fall into emotional traps; most tools predict markets or log P&L rather than explain behavior.
record.one_line_pitch: Analyzes uploaded trade history for behavioral biases like revenge trading using heuristics, logistic regression, an LLM classifier and an AI coach.
record.problem_statement: Existing trading tools focus on markets, not on the psychological patterns that drive traders to lose money.

glance.what: Standard that lets LLMs control several robots and devices at once from voice or text prompts.
glance.why: Gives AI a physical body by letting prompts drive many hardware platforms together.

record.what_it_is: An SDK and protocol, like MCP but for physical devices, where a JSON description of a hardware node is turned into a TCP pub/sub layer so an LLM can discover and control it. Demoed as a voice-driven chef robot using an SO-ARM101 arm and a camera.
record.problem_and_user: Builders wanting LLMs to act in the physical world; the motivating example is a household assistant that prepares food.
record.one_line_pitch: SDK and protocol letting LLMs discover and control hardware nodes over a custom TCP pub/sub layer, demoed with an inverse-kinematics robot arm that picks ingredients.
record.problem_statement: LLMs lack a standard way to sense and act in the physical world, such as household tasks like preparing food.
record.devpost_tagline: Giving AI a physical embodiment for the world. Control multiple hardware platforms cooperatively via LLM prompts. Deployed with a custom voice-activated autonomous chef robot.
devpost_first_sections: Overview Model Context Protocol (MCP) revolutionized the capabilities of LLMs by offering a radically new way of creating software for our everyday lives. Missing from this was meaningful capability to interact with the real world beyond a screen, and inspired us to develop our Hardware Context Protocol (HCP). It enables LLMs to control hardware components via well-defined exposed interfaces, allowing AI to interact with the world through reading sensor data, commanding actuators, and bringing them all together with context. The problem that inspired us was household serving (or rather, the lack of an intelligent machine to do so) - think making salads, finding snacks. We proved that our HCP

We created an SDK that allows the user to create a minimal JSON-based definition of a certain hardware node and what actions it exposes to the LLM. This then bootstraps a custom TCP networking layer deployable on the hardware node compliant with our novel HCP interaction layer. The LLM goes through an initial discovery period where any HCP-bootstrapped TCP nodes are able to subscribe to it and pass relevant context in the HCP-defined schema. Sensors, like a camera, can detect the locations of objects and items of interest within their sensing frame, exposing them to the model; these can then be used to inform control actions orchestrated by the HCP.

glance.what: Tool that streamlines Caterpillar's equipment inspection process.
glance.why: Makes Caterpillar equipment inspections faster and more streamlined.

record.problem_statement: Field heavy-equipment inspections use inconsistent checklists and poor records.
record.devpost_tagline: Caterpillar inspection process streamlined.

The name plays on "inspect"—because we're making the entire process effortless and reliable. Through the simplified inspection process, we can perform inspections more frequently, increasing the probability of discovering critical defects.

glance.why: Helps elderly and non-English users find the right on-screen element just by asking.

record.problem_and_user: Older adults, non-English speakers and non-technical users who can't find on-screen controls such as unmute or camera in video calls; inspired by the creators' grandparents.
record.one_line_pitch: macOS menu-bar assistant that hears a spoken request, detects on-screen UI elements, and highlights what to click with spoken directions.
record.target_user: older adults and non-technical computer users
record.problem_statement: Older adults and non-technical users struggle to find the right controls in complex apps such as video calls.
record.devpost_tagline: Accent is a macOS accessibility tool for elderly and non-English users that gives LLMs sight with a CV UI classifier. Users ask what to do and get the right UI element highlighted in real time.
devpost_first_sections: From our grandparents struggling to unmute and flip their cameras, we built Accent the accessibility agent that highlights specific UI to navigate in real time. Our goal is to make technology more learnable, approachable, and intuitive for everyone.

Accent is a local macOS assistant that lets you press a keyboard shortcut, ask what you want to do on screen, and get a highlighted UI element plus verbal directions. A user can say something specific like “Call my daughter” or “Turn on subtitles,” or something more vague like “Why can’t you hear me?” or “I want the words on my screen,” in any language! glance.why: Makes technology usable across different disabilities instead of one standard form.

record.problem_statement: Computer interfaces assume hand use, clear speech or sight, excluding many people with disabilities.

glance.what: Tool for exploring and visualizing data patterns.
glance.why: Unclear; the tagline 'Data is power' does not say what problem it solves.

record.what_it_is: A data observability system that tracks how data is created, moved and used, detects anomalies and trends with statistical models, and shows current and predicted flows in a Streamlit dashboard.
record.problem_and_user: Organizations that cannot see how data moves, risking inefficiency, security and compliance trouble; page says the problem came from the PNC challenge.
record.one_line_pitch: Data observability dashboard that tracks data flows and uses statistical models to detect anomalies and predict future data movement.
record.target_user: data and platform teams in enterprises
record.problem_statement: Organizations lack visibility into how data is created, accessed, moved and used, creating governance and security risks.
record.devpost_tagline: Data is power

Your solution should allow organizations to monitor and analyze how data is created, accessed, moved, and used – with business context.

Data Pattern Observatory combines real-time data tracking with statistical modeling to not only monitor but also predict data flow patterns. It uses historical data and statistical analysis to identify trends, detect anomalies, and predict future data movement patterns, helping organizations proactively manage their data infrastructure.

glance.what: Chapel Hill rewards app with coupons from local restaurants and shops that help small businesses.
glance.for_whom: students and visitors in Chapel Hill
glance.why: Saves students and visitors money while sending revenue to local small businesses.

Living on the college budget makes it hard to support local spots that are more often at higher price points than accessible food chains, like Chick-fil-A, Raising Cane's, and McDonald's. glance.what: Educational tool that teaches the public about natural disasters and assesses damage from specific incidents.
glance.for_whom: the general public and disaster response groups
glance.why: Helps the public learn about disasters and measure the damage each incident caused.

record.problem_and_user: Public awareness and damage assessment after disasters like California wildfires; for affected, at-risk and curious people.
record.one_line_pitch: Dashboard that educates on natural-disaster hazards and shows region-level data such as property damage and drought, motivated by the California fires.
record.problem_statement: People affected or potentially affected by wildfires need accessible information about hazards and regional impacts.
record.devpost_tagline: To educate the public about natural disasters and to assess the damages caused by specific incidents.

glance.what: VR-enhanced data center planner with 2D drag-and-drop layout and live 3D visualization.
glance.for_whom: data center planners and their clients
glance.why: Lets planners lay out and adjust data centers interactively and share them with clients.

record.problem_statement: Sales teams need to plan and show data center module layouts to clients in the real room context.

glance.what: Tool that checks whether people wash their hands with the full WHO procedure, at scale.
glance.why: Cuts infections by verifying proper hand-washing procedures across many people.

record.what_it_is: Hand-hygiene compliance system: a Raspberry Pi camera runs a CNN plus LSTM ensemble to recognise WHO hand-washing steps, an ESP8266 lights LEDs per step, and a dashboard compares units.
record.problem_and_user: Healthcare workers who often skip steps of the WHO hand-washing procedure, and hospitals wanting to verify compliance.
record.one_line_pitch: Camera-based handwashing monitor that checks WHO protocol steps and shows progress with LEDs.
record.problem_statement: Many people, including healthcare workers, skip proper handwashing steps, risking infection.
record.devpost_tagline: Only 1/3 of doctors wash their hands with the full WHO procedure, contributing to infections in over 1/7 middle income households. We make it easy to validate proper sanitation procedures at scale.
devpost_first_sections: One time my dentist handled the tools from the previous patient, then only quickly rinsed their hands before operating on me. I was worried whether their hands were completely clean. Turns out a vast majority of people including healthcare workers do not wash their hands in the correct manner, so we decided to bring change to how people wash their hands. In this project, we use computer vision to check if all areas of the hand are thoroughly cleaned, according to the procedure recommended by the WHO.

Our product checks that the complete WHO protocol is followed to ensure a clean environment in healthcare locations. As you wash your hands, there will be visual feedback if you are following the steps correctly. A blinking green LED will signify which step it detects and a solid green LED signifies that the step has been completed. A blinking LED will only become solid after the step has been done for a sufficient duration. After each wash, the overall performance is uploaded to the website deltawash.tech. deltawash.tech serves as a dashboard to evaluate compliance across different units and to identify commonly missed steps.

devpost_first_sections: Product managers spend too much time buried in documentation, research, and coordination — not actual strategy. We wanted to change that. For a physician, an incorrect or unfamiliar record can become a reputational and administrative burden, especially when there is a limited review and dispute window. We saw an opportunity to transform a traditionally low-conversion cold-outbound problem into a genuinely useful, physician-first experience. FalsePay is an HCP engagement and Open Payments audit platform that helps teams identify potentially questionable payment records, enrich physician information from the live CMS NPPES registry, and provide physicians with a secure, low-friction audit experience. The platform brings together five key workflows: Live NPI enrichment : Search a 10-digit NPI and retrieve verified physician details from the CMS NPPES Registry, including legal name, credentials, primary taxonomy, and practice location. glance.what: IoT pill bottle that tracks medication use and shows adherence in a web dashboard.
glance.for_whom: patients on long-term medication and medical researchers
glance.why: Helps patients take prescribed medication on schedule, cutting costly non-adherence.

record.what_it_is: A smart pill bottle with a load cell and ESP32 that detects pill removal, plus a Next.js dashboard showing patient profile, dosing windows, adherence percentage, anomalies, pill-count trends and an event log.
record.problem_and_user: Clinicians, caregivers and researchers tracking medication adherence; cites 30-50% non-adherence and $100-300B yearly cost.
record.one_line_pitch: Sensor-equipped smart pill bottle that streams pill-count data to a web dashboard showing adherence scores and anomalies.
record.problem_statement: Many chronic patients skip prescribed doses, costing the healthcare system heavily and muddying clinical trial data.
record.devpost_tagline: Modern care in a bottle - IOT medication tracker + web dashboard
devpost_first_sections: Medication non-adherence is a silent but massive issue. Studies show that 30–50% of patients with chronic conditions fail to follow their prescribed regimens, and nearly half of study participants intentionally skip doses. The impact is staggering: non-adherence costs the U.S. healthcare system an estimated $100–$300 billion annually in avoidable expenses. Dose was born from the need for a smarter, scalable solution to address this challenge.

Dose is a smart medication adherence system that pairs a sensor-enabled pill bottle with an interactive web dashboard. The pill bottle uses a load cell sensor to detect pill movements in real time, producing an accurate, tamper-resistant record of medication usage. On the software side, the dashboard visualizes this data with patient profiles, adherence scores, dosing windows, anomaly detection, and pill count trends. By uniting reliable hardware with intuitive analytics, Dose empowers clinicians, caregivers, and researchers to monitor adherence, reduce trial errors, and ultimately improve patient outcomes.
